# Set-up

This markdown performs doublet calling using scDblFinder on the whole, uncorrected Tonsil 10x Flex dataset. This includes:

- removal of low quality cells 

- scDblFinder doublet calling, split per sample

- clustering (using Seurat)

- export of results as `qs2` object, as well as in 10X cellranger output format

## Load data

Note that the following code chunk was previously run by Gunjan Dixit, and the resulting rds object was loaded for the remaining analysis. 

`cellranger multi` filtered matrices for each sample (n=16) were loaded and combined into a SingleCellExperiment. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}

#Lists for sample names. Used in loading the CellRanger outputs.
batch_samples <- list.dirs("/oshlack_lab/shared/projects/paed-airway-atlas/G000231_Neeland_batch9/extdata/CellRanger/G000231_batch9_1/outs/per_sample_outs", full.names = FALSE, recursive = F)

#Helper functions for reading the per-sample counts into a SingleCellExperiment object.
make_filtered_sce <- function(sample_name) {
  print(sample_name)
  counts <- Read10X_h5(sprintf('/oshlack_lab/shared/projects/paed-airway-atlas/G000231_Neeland_batch9/extdata/CellRanger/G000231_batch9_1/outs/per_sample_outs/%s/count/sample_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5', sample_name))
  sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = c("counts" = counts))
  sce$Sample <- sample_name
  return(sce)
}

sce <- lapply(batch_samples, function(sn) make_filtered_sce(sn))
sce <- sce_cbind(sce_list = sce,
                 exprs = "counts",
                 cut_off_batch = 0, #keep everything
                 cut_off_overall = 0, #keep everything
                 colData_names = "Sample") #merge, no integration

```


```{r, include=FALSE}
sce <- readRDS(here("data/Tonsils_10xFlex/G000231_Neeland_batch9_Tonsils.CellRanger_filtered.SCE.rds"))

```


# QC filtering 

Low quality cells will be removed prior to performing doublet detection. Our main goal here is to eliminate cells with a very low library size and/or number of genes detected, as well as cells with unusually high % mitochondrial reads as their presence may interfere with doublet calling. 10X flex does not have any probes for ribosomal genes. 


Add per cell summary metrics

```{r}
is.mito <- grepl(pattern = "^MT", rownames(sce))
sce <- addPerCellQCMetrics(sce, subsets = list(mito = is.mito))

new_meta <- sce@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% #immediately clean up metadata
  dplyr::rename(., nfeatures = detected, ncount = sum) %>%
  select(., -c("subsets_mito_sum", "subsets_mito_detected", "total"))
sce@colData <- new_meta %>% DataFrame()

```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(new_meta, is.mito); gc()
```


Plot distribution of library sizes, detected genes and %mito, split for each sample. The dotted lines indicate selected thresholds. 

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
p1 <- plotColData(
    sce,
    "ncount",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 200,
               linetype = "dotted")

p2 <- plotColData(
    sce,
    "nfeatures",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 150,
               linetype = "dotted")
  
p3 <- plotColData(
    sce,
    "subsets_mito_percent",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 7,
               linetype = "dotted")

p1+p2+p3 + plot_layout(ncol=2)
```


Remove cells. 

```{r}
sce$high_quality_cell <- (sce$ncount >= 200) & (sce$nfeatures >= 150)  & (sce$subsets_mito_percent <= 7) 

sce@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  group_by(Sample,high_quality_cell) %>% 
  summarise(count = n()) %>% 
  group_by(Sample) %>% 
  mutate(., percent_kept = round(count/sum(count),5)) %>% 
  filter(., high_quality_cell == FALSE) %>% 
  select(Sample, count, percent_kept) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(removed_cell=count) %>% 
  knitr::kable() 

```

```{r}
sce_filtered <- sce[rowSums(counts(sce)) > 50, sce$high_quality_cell == T] #also remove genes that are barely expressed
sce_filtered
```

Plot distributions post filtering

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
p1 <- plotColData(
    sce_filtered,
    "ncount",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) 

p2 <- plotColData(
    sce_filtered,
    "nfeatures",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) 
  
p3 <- plotColData(
    sce_filtered,
    "subsets_mito_percent",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

p1+p2+p3 + plot_layout(ncol=2)
```


```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(sce, p1, p2, p3, cells_to_keep);gc()
```


# Doublet calling - scDblFinder

Running scDblFinder for doublet detection. We have already removed cells with very low library size and very high mitochondrial content. scDblFinder requires a standard workflow to be run on the SCE. As recommended by the authors, we are applying scDblFinder for each sample separately by using the `samples` parameter. 

```{r}
#standard workflow
sce_filtered <- logNormCounts(sce_filtered) %>%
  runPCA() %>%
  runUMAP()

#scDblFinder
set.seed(1997)
sce_filtered <- scDblFinder(sce_filtered,
                   clusters = T,
                   dbr.sd = 1, #removing doublet rate assumption 
                   samples = "Sample", 
                   verbose=F) 
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
gc()
```


# Clustering 

`Seurat` clustering functions are faster and more user-friendly. 

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
seu <- as.Seurat(sce_filtered, counts = "counts", data = "logcounts") #convert to seurat
gc()

# run clustering for multiple solutions, all high level
seu <- FindNeighbors(seu, reduction = "PCA", dims = 1:30, verbose=F) %>%
  FindClusters(resolution = seq(0.1, 0.3, by = 0.1), algorithm = 3, verbose=F)

#add back to SCE
sce_filtered$clustering_res0.1 <- seu$RNA_snn_res.0.1
sce_filtered$clustering_res0.2 <- seu$RNA_snn_res.0.2
sce_filtered$clustering_res0.3 <- seu$RNA_snn_res.0.3
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(seu);gc()
```

# Clean up metadata

Before we export the data, lets tidy up the metadata. 

```{r}
new_meta <- sce_filtered@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(., c("Sample", "ncount", "nfeatures", "subsets_mito_percent", "sizeFactor", "scDblFinder.class", "scDblFinder.score", "clustering_res0.1", "clustering_res0.2", "clustering_res0.3"))
sce_filtered@colData <- new_meta %>% DataFrame()

```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(new_meta);gc()
```


# Export

## qs2 export

Exporting whole object.

```{r}
filename <- here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Tonsils_10xFlex_whole_dataset_processed_scdblfinder.qs2")
qs_save(object = sce_filtered, file = filename)
```

## 10x v3 folder format whole dataset

Using the cellranger output format also saves a lot of space and allows us to load in specific things we need, such as just the metadata, or just barcodes. 

```{r}
DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Tonsils_10xFlex_whole_dataset_processed/"),
                               x = counts(sce_filtered),
                               version = "3")
#export metadata
write_tsv(x=as.data.frame(sce_filtered@colData), file=here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Tonsils_10xFlex_whole_dataset_processed/metadata.tsv"))

```


## 10x v3 folder format per sample 

We require them for each sample to run the 4 selected doublet detection tools (scDblFinder, scds, DoubletDetection, scrublet) on each sample individually. We will require the results of these doublet callers when generating the engineered tonsil dataset. We will not require the metadata for each sample individually. 

```{r, warning=FALSE}
output_dir <- here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Samples")

for (sample in sce_filtered$Sample %>% unique()){
  out_dir_tmp <- sprintf("%s/%s", output_dir, sample)
  print(out_dir_tmp)
  sce_subset <- sce_filtered[,sce_filtered$Sample == sample]
  #export counts
  DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = out_dir_tmp,
                               x = counts(sce_subset),
                               version = "3")
  rm(out_dir_tmp, sce_subset);gc()
}

```
